stem: What is the largest population to which the results of the survey can be generalized?
stimulus: The Harrowgate Storytelling Guild has 1,400 members, all of whom live in Lowfield County. A folklorist obtained a list of the guild's members who are 60 years of age or older and randomly selected 200 people from that list. Each selected member was asked whether they had first learned most of their tales from a grandparent. Of the 200 members surveyed, 126 answered yes.
choices: Only the 200 guild members who were surveyed
All guild members who are 60 years of age or older
All members of the Harrowgate Storytelling Guild
All storytellers in Lowfield County aged 60 or older
explanation: The 200 members were randomly selected from one list: guild members aged 60 or older. A random sample can speak for the group it was drawn from, so the results reach all guild members who are 60 or older. They do not reach younger members, who could not be chosen, or storytellers outside the guild.

A.why: You decided a sample can never speak for anything larger than itself. That is wrong when the sample was randomly selected. Random selection is exactly what lets you generalize to the group the sample came from.

C.why: You dropped the age qualifier. Only members aged 60 or older were on the list the sample came from, so younger guild members had no chance of being chosen.

D.why: You kept the age qualifier but widened the group from guild members to every storyteller in the county. Storytellers outside the guild were never part of the group sampled.

stem: What is the largest population to which the results of the study can be generalized?
stimulus: Westbrook Hospital posted a notice inviting its night-shift employees to take part in a study of a sleep-hygiene program. The first 150 employees to reply were enrolled. The researchers then randomly assigned 75 of the enrolled employees to complete the program and the other 75 to continue their usual routines. After 8 weeks, the employees who completed the program reported sleeping an average of 40 minutes more per day than the employees who did not.
choices: All night-shift employees at Westbrook Hospital
All employees, on any shift, at Westbrook Hospital
All night-shift health care workers in the region
Only the 150 night-shift employees in the study
explanation: Random assignment to the program lets you draw a conclusion about cause, but only for the people who were studied. The 150 employees were the first to volunteer. They were not randomly selected from the night-shift staff, so they may differ from night-shift employees who did not reply. The results apply only to the 150 employees in the study.

A.why: You took random assignment to mean random selection. The treatment groups were assigned at random, but the participants were the first 150 volunteers. They were not a random sample of the hospital's night-shift staff, so you cannot generalize to that staff.

B.why: You went beyond the night-shift staff to every shift. Only night-shift employees were invited, and even they were not randomly selected.

C.why: You chose the broadest group because it sounds the most impressive. The volunteers all came from one hospital and were not randomly selected, so the results cannot reach workers across the region.

stem: What is the largest population to which the results shown in the table can be generalized?
stimulus:
The Ashgrove Printmakers' Cooperative has 600 members. A researcher randomly selected 120 members of the cooperative and recorded each member's primary printmaking technique and the number of juried exhibitions the member had entered. The table shows the results for only the selected members who had entered at least 3 juried exhibitions.

Primary Technique of Selected Members with at Least 3 Juried Exhibitions
Technique | Number of members
Etching | 9
Woodcut | 14
Screenprint | 11
Lithograph | 6
choices: All cooperative members with at least 3 juried exhibitions
All members of the Ashgrove Printmakers' Cooperative
Only the 40 selected members with at least 3 exhibitions
All printmakers who have entered at least 3 juried exhibitions
explanation: The 120 members were randomly selected from the whole cooperative. The table, however, shows only the selected members who had entered at least 3 juried exhibitions. Those 40 members are effectively a random sample of the cooperative members who meet that threshold. The table's results therefore reach all cooperative members with at least 3 juried exhibitions, and no further.

B.why: You dropped the threshold. The sample came from the whole cooperative, but the table includes only members with at least 3 juried exhibitions. Its results describe that subgroup, not every member.

C.why: You assumed a sample can describe only itself. These members came from a random sample of the cooperative, so the table can speak for all cooperative members who meet the same threshold.

D.why: You kept the threshold but widened the group to every printmaker. Only members of the Ashgrove cooperative could have been selected.

stem: What is the largest population to which the results of the study can be generalized?
stimulus: The Calder Rift monitoring network has 900 seismic stations. A seismologist made a list of the network's stations that are located above an elevation of 1,000 meters and were installed before 2005. She randomly selected 60 stations from this list and checked each one's sensor calibration. She found that 18 of the 60 stations had sensors that recorded ground motion at least 5 percent too low.
choices: All Calder Rift stations located above 1,000 meters
All Calder Rift stations installed before 2005
All Calder Rift stations above 1,000 meters installed before 2005
Only the 60 Calder Rift stations that were checked
explanation: The 60 stations were randomly selected from a list with two qualifiers: an elevation above 1,000 meters and installation before 2005. The results can be generalized to every station in the network that meets both conditions. Stations that fail either condition could not have been selected.

A.why: You kept the elevation qualifier but dropped the installation date. Stations above 1,000 meters that were installed in 2005 or later were not on the list, and newer equipment could be calibrated differently.

B.why: You kept the installation date but dropped the elevation qualifier. Stations at or below 1,000 meters were never eligible to be selected.

D.why: You assumed the results describe only the stations that were checked. The 60 stations were a random sample from the list, so the results extend to every station on that list.

stem: What is the largest population to which the results of the study can be generalized?
stimulus: The Varden Museum holds 1,200 fossil leaves collected from the Brennan Quarry. Of these, 500 date to the Eocene epoch. A paleobotanist randomly selected 40 of the museum's 500 Eocene leaves from the Brennan Quarry. She then randomly assigned 20 of the 40 leaves to be cleaned with an acid wash and the other 20 to be cleaned with an air-abrasion tool. Leaves cleaned with the air-abrasion tool showed a greater percentage of visible leaf pores, on average, than leaves cleaned with the acid wash.
choices: All Brennan Quarry fossil leaves held by the museum
All Eocene Brennan Quarry fossil leaves held by the museum
All Eocene fossil leaves found at the Brennan Quarry
Only the 40 Eocene fossil leaves used in the study
explanation: The 40 leaves were randomly selected from one group: the museum's 500 Eocene leaves from the Brennan Quarry. Because the cleaning methods were also randomly assigned, the results about the two methods can be generalized to that whole group of 500 leaves. They cannot be generalized to leaves from other epochs or to fossils that are not in the museum's collection.

A.why: You dropped the Eocene qualifier. The sample was drawn only from the 500 Eocene leaves, not from all 1,200 Brennan Quarry leaves in the museum.

C.why: You went beyond the museum's collection. Eocene leaves still at the quarry, or held by other collections, could not have been selected.

D.why: You assumed the results describe only the 40 leaves that were studied. Those leaves were a random sample of the museum's Eocene Brennan Quarry leaves, so the results reach that whole group.
